angles: Cloud agent workflow architectures: Codex's cloud/async execution model vs Claude Code's terminal-first approach vs Cursor's IDE-native background agents — each represents a fundamentally different design philosophy about where coding agents should live and how developers interact with them

The three-tier approval spectrum: Codex CLI graduated approval (Suggest→Auto-Edit→Full Auto) vs Claude Code's per-action prompts vs Cursor's Preview/Review loop — the safety-autonomy trade-off determines which teams can adopt which tool for CI/CD

Open-source vs proprietary lock-in: Codex CLI (Apache 2.0) and Gemini CLI (Apache 2.0) allow full code audit and customization; Claude Code and Cursor are proprietary, tying users to vendor ecosystems despite stronger agentic capabilities

The GitHub ecosystem moat: GitHub Copilot cloud agent connects from Issues, Jira, Linear, Slack, Teams, VS Code, and CLI — offering context-portability that standalone CLI tools can't match for team workflows

Pricing trap analysis: Cursor's $20/mo Pro and Background Agents 20% surcharge vs Claude Code's $100-200/mo Max tiers vs Codex CLI effectively free with ChatGPT Plus — which is cheapest depends on usage patterns, not headline prices

Developer profile fit: solo devs on a budget (Codex CLI with ChatGPT sub) vs power users needing maximum codebase understanding (Claude Code) vs teams wanting workflow-native cloud agents (Cursor/GitHub Copilot)

Benchmark trust gap: SWE-Bench Verified shows near-parity (~80%) among all three, but real-world differentiation is in context handling, CI/CD integration, error rates, and cost — not benchmark scores

Enterprise maturity battle: Cursor holds SOC 2 Type II; Claude Code has $1B+ ARR with Stripe/Wiz/Ramp case studies; Codex CLI backed by OpenAI/GitHub enterprise ecosystem — security certifications and compliance features are the real differentiator for regulated industries

GitHub Copilot vs Cursor vs Claude Code
outline: Introduction: The Cloud Agent Workflow Era — Why the Architecture of Where Agents Run Matters More Than What Model They Use
The Three Cloud Agent Architectures
Codex CLI GA: Cloud-Native, CI/CD-First Design
— Open-source (Apache 2.0) Rust + TypeScript foundation
— Three-tier approval model and Docker sandbox
— Native GitHub Actions CI/CD integration
— Cloud/async execution for background task delegation
— Multi-model support (GPT-5-Codex, Codex-Spark, o3)
Claude Code: Terminal-First with Agent Teams
— Proprietary TypeScript, agentic search, multi-file coherence
— Agent Teams orchestration for collaborative task execution
— Compaction API for infinite conversation sessions
— No native cloud agent mode — designed for local terminal use
— $1B ARR, Stripe/Wiz/Ramp production case studies
Cursor: IDE-Native with Background + Cloud Agents
— VS Code fork with $2B+ ARR, 1M+ DAU
— Background Agents (local) + Cloud Agents with Computer Use (Feb 2026)
— Preview/Review approval loop vs automatic execution
— 20% MAX surcharge model for background agent usage
— SOC 2 Type II certified, Fortune 500 adoption
GitHub Copilot Cloud Agent: The Ecosystem Play
— Asynchronous execution on GitHub in ephemeral Actions environments
— Context portability: Issues, Slack, Teams, Jira, Linear, CLI, VS Code
— Custom agents, MCP servers, Copilot Memory for specialization
— 59-min session limit, one branch at a time, GitHub-only repos
— Usage-based billing via Actions minutes + AI credits
Benchmark & Performance Analysis
— SWE-Bench Verified: Claude Code 80.8% > Gemini 80.6% > Codex 80.0%
— Terminal-Bench 2.0: Codex 77.3% > Gemini 68.5% > Claude 65.4%
— Real-world speed: Codex 45s for Dockerfile vs Claude 90s (but more thorough)
— Error rates: Claude < Codex < Gemini (consistent across sources)
Pricing in 2026: Headline Rates vs Real-World Cost
— Cursor $20/mo Pro + 20% Background Agent surcharge = $24-100/mo for heavy users
— Claude Code $20/mo Pro (limited) to $100-200/mo Max tiers
— Codex CLI effectively free with ChatGPT Plus ($20/mo) or API pay-per-use
— GitHub Copilot cloud agent: Actions + AI credits on top of Copilot sub
— The real cost depends on agent-loop multiplier — not headline rates
Safety, Security & Compliance
— Codex CLI Docker sandboxing offers strongest isolation
— Claude Code per-action permission prompts (no sandbox)
— Cursor Preview/Review + SOC 2 Type II
— GitHub Copilot protects via Actions isolation + audit trails
Decision Framework: Which Tool for Which Team Profile
— Solo devs on a budget: Codex CLI (free with ChatGPT Plus)
— Power users needing maximum codebase intelligence: Claude Code
— Teams wanting workflow-native cloud agents: Cursor Cloud Agents
— Enterprises needing async delegation: GitHub Copilot cloud agent
— CI/CD pipeline automation: Codex CLI (native GitHub Actions)
— Multi-file architectural refactoring: Claude Code (Agent Teams)
Future Outlook: Convergence and Differentiation
— All three converging on cloud agent execution models
— GitHub Copilot positioning as agent platform + marketplace
— Cursor cloud agents evolving toward full async
— Claude Code may need cloud agents to compete
— Market projected $6B→$43.8B by 2036
Conclusion: Don't Pick One, Route Across All Three
— Model routing strategy: different agents for different workflow stages
— Fast tier (formatting/edits) vs Standard tier (most coding) vs Premium tier (architecture)
— The era of a single best AI coding tool is over
